SJRES 121.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "Oil and Natural Gas Sector Climate Review: Extension of Deadlines in Standards of Performance for New, Reconstructed, and Modified Sources and Emissions Guidelines for Existing Sources".

description.summary: Disapproves the Environmental Protection Agency rule titled "Oil and Natural Gas Sector Climate Review: Extension of Deadlines in Standards of Performance for New, Reconstructed, and Modified Sources and Emissions Guidelines for Existing Sources" under chapter 8 of title 5 (the Congressional Review Act). The resolution is limited to that specific EPA rule — it addresses the agency's extensions of deadlines in standards of performance for new, reconstructed, or modified oil and gas sources and the emissions guidelines for existing sources, and thus applies to the federal regulatory action nationwide and to the oil and natural gas facilities covered by those standards and guidelines.

impact.summary: This joint resolution would use the Congressional Review Act (chapter 8 of title 5) to overturn an Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) rule that extended deadlines for complying with Standards of Performance for new, reconstructed, and modified sources and for Emissions Guidelines for existing sources in the oil and natural gas sector. If enacted, it would nullify that EPA deadline-extension and therefore directly affect the EPA (by reversing the rule), oil and natural gas companies and operators (for example, well operators, compressor and processing-plant owners, and pipeline companies) who face those standards, and state environmental agencies that implement EPA emissions-guideline plans. Under the Congressional Review Act, the disapproval would also generally bar the EPA from issuing a substantially similar rule without new congressional authorization.
